## 7a8926bd9d9f

**Classification: reproduced validator and exact-control defects; target left unchanged.** Generator SHA-256 `3159c9b3a39d6992342525082632fcd2d341c4e5474ac12a9c7a090185a7b454`.

The advertised `texture="axis_aligned"` fixture places two same-color cells in one row. `self_check` returns `[]` even though the task invariants require diagonally opposite corners. Canonical Racket execution is an identity on this input, so the accepted fixture is a no-op lesson rather than a rectangle-completion lesson. Reproducer: `checks/audit/7a8926bd9d9f/input.json`; source-bound Racket result: `checks/audit/7a8926bd9d9f/racket.json`; summarized probe: `checks/audit/7a8926bd9d9f/probe.json`.

Exact-control testing also found that `n_rects=1` and `n_rects=8` produced byte-identical grids on 300/300 paired draws (100 per band), and both requests violated their requested rectangle count on 300/300 draws. `palette_kind="warm"`, `texture="warm"`, and the unoverridden call were likewise byte-identical on all 300 draws. The implementation draws `"rectangles"` rather than the advertised `"n_rects"` key and never consumes either helpful palette axis. This is a concrete training-stratification defect, not only a documentation mismatch.

Racket command, packet-root cwd: `python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 7a8926bd9d9f --input ../checks/audit/7a8926bd9d9f/input.json --out ../checks/audit/7a8926bd9d9f/racket.json` (exit 0). No fix was made because this was an audit-only target.
